name: Styrenix Performance Materials Ltd (formerly INEOS Styrolution India)
tagline: India's dominant styrenics (ABS/SAN/polystyrene) producer, now Agarwal-family-controlled again post the ISAPL/INEOS exit, mid-way through a capacity-doubling program - but management itself has flagged the Q1 FY27 margin/PAT surge as an abnormal, non-recurring spike (Strait-of-Hormuz supply disruption), with volumes actually down 26% YoY, so the 'cheap on an annualised Q1 run-rate' framing does not survive a fresh filings read.
business_overview: Styrenix Performance Materials (renamed from INEOS Styrolution India after the global JV exited) manufactures styrenics - ABS, SAN, polystyrene and specialty styrenic polymers - for automotive, appliances, packaging and consumer-durable customers. Following the promoter/ownership realignment (the Agarwal family, via Shiva Performance Materials Pvt Ltd, reacquired control from the erstwhile ISAPL/INEOS structure, releasing all pledged shares by 2024), the company is mid-way through a capacity expansion (ABS Phase I, ~50,000 TPA, ~Rs 350 Cr, internal accruals, commissioning within FY27, first full-year contribution FY28), addressing an import-substitution opportunity as LG Polymers' India ABS capacity shut down, leaving only Styrenix and Supreme Petrochem as the major domestic suppliers against ~130-140k tonnes of imports in a ~275k-tonne market. Seeded 2026-09-13 via untrusted X triage (@rajuidesai, medium conviction).
fundamentals_table: ROCE ~13.8%; ROE ~14.2% (latest TTM, consolidated - includes the abnormal Q1 FY27 quarter; prior data-file figures of 16.8%/21.45% were an earlier, higher snapshot)
FY26 consolidated revenue growth ~9% YoY (TTM); 5-yr revenue CAGR ~11.69% - a price/mix-driven business, not a volume-growth one

Q1 FY27 standalone EBITDA margin 26.1% vs 11.9% YoY - but management explicitly called this an 'abnormal snapshot' (Strait-of-Hormuz supply disruption) and guided 10-12% as the realistic sustainable baseline; FY26 full-year consolidated EBITDA margin was ~10.4%, in line with that guided baseline
Q1 FY27 standalone revenue Rs 770.5 Cr (+6.6% YoY, price/mix-driven); PAT Rs 137.3 Cr (+150.3% YoY); but standalone sales VOLUME fell 26% YoY to 38.9kt (consolidated volume -24% YoY to 50.8kt)
46.24% promoter holding (Jun 2026), down from 62.73% (Mar 2024) - tracks the disclosed 2024 INEOS-to-Agarwal ownership restructuring, not a stealth exit; 0% pledged throughout
Rs 1,773 - Rs 3,524 - stock hit fresh 52-week lows (~Rs 1,773-1,836) in Jan-Mar 2026 after a weak Dec-2025 quarter, before the Q1 FY27 spread-driven beat lifted it back to ~Rs 2,050-2,070
fundamentals_narrative: Re-verified against fresh filings, this is a materially more cautious picture than the prior pass: Q1 FY27's headline EBITDA margin doubling (11.9% -> 26.1%) and PAT surge (~2.5x) were explicitly characterised by management on the concall as an 'abnormal snapshot' driven by a temporary supply-chain disruption (Strait of Hormuz-related feedstock/logistics dislocation widening styrene-monomer spreads), not a structural re-rating - management's own stated sustainable baseline is 10-12% EBITDA margin, close to FY26's actual full-year consolidated 10.4%. Critically, standalone sales VOLUME fell 26% YoY in Q1 FY27 (38.9kt vs ~52.6kt), meaning the revenue growth (+6.6%) was entirely price/spread-driven while underlying demand momentum weakened - this cuts against the 'import-substitution volume story' framing used in the earlier pass. The stock's 'cheap at ~6-7x annualised Q1 run-rate' claim from the prior pass does not survive: annualising an abnormal, management-disavowed quarter is not a valid run-rate; on FY26's actual (normalized-ish) PAT of Rs 182.8 Cr against a ~Rs 3,600-3,900 Cr market cap, the stock trades at a much more pedestrian ~19-21x, and even blending in a partial Q1 FY27 benefit still lands well above the '6-7x' figure. Debt remains low (debt/EBITDA ~0.4x) and the ABS Phase I capacity expansion (~50,000 TPA, ~Rs 350 Cr) remains on schedule for FY27 commissioning with first full-year contribution in FY28 - a genuine, funded, on-track commitment. Promoter holding has declined from 62.73% (Mar 2024) to 46.24% (Jun 2026), consistent with the known ownership restructuring rather than a fresh exit signal, and pledge has stayed at 0% throughout.
technical_read: Stock round-tripped from a fresh 52-week low (~Rs 1,773-1,836, Jan-Mar 2026, on a weak Dec-2025 quarter) back up to ~Rs 2,050-2,070 (Sep 2026) on the Q1 FY27 spread-driven beat - still ~41-49% below the Rs 3,524 high. Not independently re-verified against the 30W EMA this pass.

Promoter holding decline (62.73% -> 46.24% since Mar 2024) is the known, disclosed INEOS-to-Agarwal restructuring, not accompanied by any pledge increase.
bull_case: Dominant domestic styrenics/ABS producer benefiting from a genuine import-substitution tailwind (LG Polymers' India ABS capacity shut, leaving Styrenix and Supreme Petrochem as the main domestic suppliers against a large import base ~130-140kt of a ~275kt market)
ABS Phase I capacity expansion (~50,000 TPA, ~Rs 350 Cr, internal accruals) is on schedule for FY27 commissioning, first full-year contribution FY28 - a real, funded, on-track commitment

bear_case: Commodity petrochemical business - margins are spread-driven (styrene-monomer/ABS spreads) and management itself confirmed Q1 FY27's 26.1% margin was a one-off 'abnormal snapshot', not a durable re-rating; sustainable baseline guided at 10-12% (FY26 actual was 10.4%)

Standalone sales VOLUME fell 26% YoY in Q1 FY27 (and consolidated volume -24% YoY) - revenue growth was purely price/spread driven, undercutting the volume-led import-substitution narrative in the near term

The prior pass's '~6-7x cheap on annualised Q1 run-rate' valuation claim does not hold up: annualising a management-disavowed abnormal quarter overstates sustainable earnings; on FY26 actual PAT the stock is closer to ~19-21x, a materially less compelling entry point
5-yr revenue CAGR of only ~11.69% and FY26 growth ~9% - this remains a margin-rerating story, not a volume-growth story; a mature, cyclical commodity TAM caps the realistic upside magnitude
Stock still ~41-49% below its 52-week high despite the Q1 FY27 beat - the market has not fully re-rated the story, which could reflect skepticism about margin durability rather than an opportunity
Promoter holding down from 62.73% to 46.24% over the past ~2.5 years (disclosed restructuring, but a real, sizeable reduction in promoter skin-in-the-game nonetheless)
verdict_headline: Genuine import-substitution positioning and an on-schedule capacity expansion in Indian styrenics, but a fresh filings read shows the Q1 FY27 margin/PAT surge that drove the earlier bull case was explicitly management-disavowed as a one-off spread spike (volumes actually fell 26% YoY) and the 'cheap' valuation claim does not survive using FY26's real run-rate. Conviction downgraded Medium -> Low-Medium; thesis_fit stays 'neither' on a four_box score of 2.5.
verdict_reasoning: four_box re-derived at 2.5 (tailwind yes - import-substitution/capacity dynamic still structurally real; tam weak - mature, cyclical commodity petrochemical market; moat weak - dominant domestic scale post LG Polymers exit but still a commodity spread/price-taker business; valuation moved from 'yes' to 'weak' - the prior pass's ~6-7x figure relied on annualising an abnormal quarter management itself disavowed; on FY26's real ~Rs 182.8 Cr consolidated PAT the stock is closer to ~19-21x, not obviously cheap). 2.5 sits in the 2.0-2.5 band, which mandates thesis_fit 'neither' with no written exception available (valuation is no longer 'yes', and growth is decelerating on a volume basis, not accelerating) - no analyst_override needed this pass since the score itself now dictates 'neither'.

Conviction downgraded from Medium to Low-Medium: the active, specific ValuePickr thread corroboration still supports staying above plain Low, but the combination of (a) management explicitly calling the headline beat an abnormal one-off, (b) a 26% YoY volume decline, and (c) valuation no longer screening cheap once the abnormal quarter is excluded, outweighs the community-signal support that previously justified Medium.

No red flag: pledge fully released and stayed at 0% throughout; ownership realignment complete and disclosed. Promoter holding decline (62.73% -> 46.24%) is the known restructuring, not accompanied by any pledge increase, so it does not trip the shareholding_pattern.concurrent_red_flag rule.

The ABS Phase I capacity expansion remains a genuine positive (on schedule, funded by internal accruals, FY27 commissioning / FY28 first full-year contribution) - this is the main forward catalyst worth tracking, distinct from the now-discredited margin-durability framing.

four_box.note: Import-substitution tailwind (LG Polymers exit) remains structurally real and explicit; TAM is a mature, cyclical commodity chemical market; moat is scale/dominance in a spread-driven commodity business, not a structural pricing moat; valuation downgraded from 'yes' to 'weak' this pass - the prior ~6-7x figure annualised an abnormal, management-disavowed Q1 FY27 quarter (volumes -26% YoY), and on FY26's real run-rate the stock trades closer to ~19-21x.
